importance_ranking.reason: High visual variation between toll booth sub-types (highway NHAI cabin vs parking cashier booth vs weighbridge cabin vs generic portable cabin). Buyers must confirm product type visually before reading any text — wrong form factor is an immediate skip.

Wall material and cabin size are non-interchangeable shortlisting gates — an ACP-clad NHAI-compliant booth cannot substitute for a PUF-insulated booth on a highway project. Listings without these specs cannot be evaluated by contractor buyers.

Every toll booth is custom-fabricated to client drawings; listed price is a budget entry point only. Indian contractor buyers are price-sensitive but final price is always negotiated per project scope — price comparison is only meaningful after spec equivalence is confirmed.

importance_ranking.brand_important_reason: No recognised consumer-facing brands exist in this category — buyers search by fabrication capability, prior NHAI project experience, and installation support, not by manufacturer name.
importance_ranking.reason: Institutional and contractor buyers evaluate the seller's fabrication track record, NHAI project history, and ability to supply with installation — seller credentials are a qualification signal after spec and price shortlisting.

importance_ranking.unit_note: Toll booth canopy structures covering multiple lanes may be quoted per project or per sq ft, but these are distinct from the cabin unit and belong to a separate product category.
importance_ranking.reason: Unit is entirely implied — every toll booth cabin is a discrete structure sold per piece. No buyer ever questions whether a fabricated cabin is sold per piece.

top_configurator_specs.reason: Defines the product class (ACP vs PUF vs FRP vs MS vs GI) with non-interchangeable compliance and thermal performance implications for NHAI highway use, and carries the largest price delta across values in this category.
Directly determines fabrication cost and structural scale — single-lane vs double-lane configurations are size-determined and non-interchangeable across project requirements.

missing_important_specs.why_important: PUF panel thickness (40mm vs 60mm vs 80mm) is an NHAI compliance and thermal comfort signal that drives significant price variation — captured only as a binary checkbox in Features, not as a configurable spec with values.
MS vs GI structural frame is a durability and corrosion-resistance differentiator for coastal and humid highway locations, and is not captured by Wall Material which covers cladding panels only.
Single vs double lane is an NHAI-specified configuration that determines cabin width, counter layout, and structural requirements — not reliably inferred from Cabin Size alone.

top_rfq_specs.reason: Defines the product class and compliance tier — sellers need material type to confirm fabrication capability and price accurately, as ACP, PUF, FRP, and MS carry fundamentally different cost structures and performance profiles.

Determines structural scale and fabrication cost — sellers need dimensions to confirm whether the requirement falls within their standard range or requires custom fabrication and to provide an accurate price.

missing_important_specs.why_important: Highway toll, parking, and weighbridge applications have distinct structural and compliance requirements — sellers need this to confirm NHAI compliance capability and appropriate fitments before responding.

Electrical fitment scope (no electrical, single phase, solar) materially affects fabrication cost and seller capability — sellers need this to price accurately and confirm they can supply the required electrical provisions.
